newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm on U.S. funds, seen firming.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm on U.S. funds, seen firming.

text.p: Russian shares edged up two percent in average volumes on Monday, pushed up in an afternoon rally which appeared to be led by U.S. fund buying of leading shares, brokers said.
The Russian Trading System gained 2.1 percent to close at 165.93 on $16.8 million volume.
Irkutsenergo was one of the leaders, closing at $0.100 after $0.096 at Friday's close. LUKoil closed at $9.17 after $9.05 and Mosenergo rose to $0.894 from $0.867 and UES to $0.0740 from $0.0725.

"The tone was positive and will probably continue over the next few days," said Brunswick's Martin Diggle. "We saw some institutional buying from the States," he said, adding that interest was centered on a few leading shares.
He said the week's rise would probably be gradual.
Another dealer said new money, including a Morgan Stanley fund, appeared poised to invest.

Lenenergo utility workers said they would not strike and the stock edged up to $0.38 from $0.37 on Friday. Brokers said the shares had not fallen significantly on the threat of a strike as foreign investors with long-term expectations ordered stock.
Retailer TSUM rose to $0.360 from $0.335 after announcing it would issue $12 million in new shares over the next two months to help cover expansion of its central Moscow store.

Komineft was flat at $1.40 after holding company NK KomiTEK announced it could sell up to 38 percent of its stock. "It's perceived as being badly managed and clients are afraid of unauthorised share dilution," said one broker.

Traders said the market was not very liquid, with President Boris Yeltsin's impending heart surgery hanging over the market for the next few weeks and that fund flow would be the primary market mover over the next few weeks.
